vision.one_line: SAP professionals clone sap-agent-context as a local, agent-first SAP context resource: compact enough to run quickly, rich enough to ground useful SAP work, and strict enough to fail closed when the repo lacks evidence.
vision.north_star: A cloneable, local-first SAP context runtime for agents: self-contained, fast, compact, evidence-backed and fail-closed.
vision.promise: A SAP professional should be able to clone this repository, run the local gates, query it with an agent, and get source-labelled context bundles for SAP functional design, field mapping, workflow, roles, migration, integrations, analytics, EAM/PM and implementation support.
vision.anti_memory_clause: The repo is useful when it gives an agent enough structured context to reason from zero without leaning on generic model memory, while still refusing to invent release, tenant, customizing, role, availability or production facts.

commands: uv run sap-agent-context query-explain --intent fo --topic "maintenance plan task list measuring point" --limit 8
expected_outcomes: the repo builds locally without external hosted retrieval services
JSONL records and generated indexes are internally consistent
the agent receives compact context, not a documentation dump
each useful answer can point to source, freshness and access boundaries
missing tenant or release evidence becomes a visible gap, not a hallucinated conclusion

principles.title: Agent-first product surface
principles.rule: Optimize for agents consuming structured context. Do not design the repo as a human browsing site, wiki, training manual, or SAP Help replacement.
bad: long prose pages that agents must scrape to recover facts
human wiki as primary product surface

principles.title: Self-contained local clone
principles.rule: A cloned repo should contain enough source-labelled metadata, schemas, tests and runtime build commands to be useful on a local machine without copying SAP proprietary documentation.
bad: external state required for basic validation

principles.title: Fast by default
principles.rule: Default workflows should complete quickly enough to stay in the development loop; heavy or optional work must be explicit.
bad: broad content campaigns that slow gates without improving retrieval
opaque hosted services as default path

principles.title: Compact, not shallow
principles.rule: High signal density beats copied documentation or vague labels. A good record is small but useful: id, kind, source, access, freshness, claim, relations, retrieval hints, caveats and test expectations.
bad: shallow labels with no evidence boundary

principles.title: Reliable means fail-closed
principles.rule: Reliability is refusing to cross an evidence boundary, not fluent SAP-sounding output.
fail_closed_on: roles and authorizations in a target system
SAP Notes/KBA/SAP for Me content without authorized verification
bad: tenant or customizing claims from generic context

principles.title: Evidence before coverage
principles.rule: More domains are not automatically progress. A small source-labelled slice with fixtures is better than many unverified records.

principles.title: JSON-first, generated-artifact JSON-only
principles.rule: records/*.jsonl is the canonical agent record surface. Generated report evidence and machine-consumable examples are JSON-only. Markdown may remain as narrative operating context for maintainers and agents, but never as generated evidence, report output or machine-readable examples.

principles.title: Retrieval is part of the product
principles.rule: A record that cannot be retrieved for the right prompt is not very useful, and a retrieval tweak that breaks nearby domains is not an improvement.
required_proof: positive fixtures or smokes that prove intended records appear near the top
negative fixtures or smokes that prove generic or nearby words do not hijack the query
bad: records that never surface for target prompts

principles.title: Public-safe by construction
principles.rule: The repo must stay cloneable and publishable.
good: source pointers instead of copied proprietary text

principles.title: Every gap should become steerable
principles.rule: A gap is useful when it is named, classified and actionable. Avoid vague backlog language like 'needs more SAP content'.
report_fields: missing source, FO pattern, rule, fixture, freshness or retrieval proof

repo_lenses.meaning: SAP objects, apps, fields, claims, sources, relations and caveats.
Local SQLite/FTS/vector read model generated from records.
From-zero SAP lenses: foundation, lifecycle, landscape, edition, release, customizing, org, process, surface and evidence.
Bundle schema, query examples, fixtures and fail-closed consumer behavior.
Reports and tests that turn unknowns into targeted follow-up tasks.

non_goals: human wiki as the primary product surface
proof that all SAP claims are globally correct

acceptance_scorecard.question: Does the change improve records, bundles, runtime behavior, tests, reports or operating context for agents?
acceptance_scorecard.pass_condition: The change improves the agent-facing product surface instead of only prose.

acceptance_scorecard.question: Can a fresh clone rebuild or consume the result locally?
acceptance_scorecard.pass_condition: Local commands and generated artifacts are reproducible from repo state.

acceptance_scorecard.question: Does the default gate stay practical, deterministic and local?
acceptance_scorecard.pass_condition: Default checks remain local and bounded.

acceptance_scorecard.question: Is the information structured and high-signal rather than copied prose?
acceptance_scorecard.pass_condition: Facts live in structured records/contracts, not only narrative text.

acceptance_scorecard.question: Are source/access/freshness/release/tenant boundaries explicit?
acceptance_scorecard.pass_condition: Evidence boundaries are visible and fail closed.

acceptance_scorecard.question: Are machine-consumable artifacts JSON/JSONL rather than Markdown?
acceptance_scorecard.pass_condition: Generated reports and examples are JSON/JSONL.

acceptance_scorecard.question: Is there no client, tenant, secret, screenshot, export or proprietary copied text?
acceptance_scorecard.pass_condition: Public-safety scan and review find no forbidden material.

acceptance_scorecard.question: Are important prompts protected by focused tests, fixtures or query smokes?
acceptance_scorecard.pass_condition: Positive and negative retrieval behavior is tested.

acceptance_scorecard.question: If something is incomplete, is it reported as an actionable gap?
acceptance_scorecard.pass_condition: Gaps are named, classified and actionable.

acceptance_scorecard.question: Does the output avoid implying exhaustive SAP certification?
acceptance_scorecard.pass_condition: Residual risk and proof boundaries are explicit.

review_checklist: Does this help SAP professionals clone the repo as a practical agent resource?
Is the product surface still agent-first rather than prose-first?
Are records/source pointers/freshness/relations explicit where facts matter?
Are generated reports and machine examples JSON-only?
Are tenant/release/customizing claims fail-closed when target evidence is missing?
Did the change add retrieval or fixture proof for important behavior?
Did the final claim state what was proven and what remains outside scope?

maturity_model.meaning: Records parse and validate, but usefulness is not proven.
Important prompts retrieve the record or bundle.
Source/access/freshness and fail-closed caveats are explicit.
Positive and negative tests protect the intended behavior.
Downstream bundle consumers can use it without hidden assumptions.

roadmap_principles: Finish JSONL-native authoring paths without breaking legacy imports.
Promote report-only domains only when fixtures and source boundaries justify it.
Improve query-explain until agents can understand why context was selected.
Turn curation reports into targeted follow-up tasks.
Prefer one deep, verified domain slice over five shallow domains.
Keep the repo cloneable, public-safe and local-first even as coverage grows.
residual_risk_wording: Residual risk: audit scope is repo-level, not exhaustive claim-by-claim SAP content review across all domain-pack YAML. Gates, runtime behavior, source/access boundaries, CI semantics and the from-zero ontology layer are covered; full SAP claim curation remains a separate pass.
